data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin octavus meaning eighth or wealthy. Octavia was a Roman woman in the New Testament who was a generous hostess and friend to the Apostle Paul. The name Octavie carries the meaning “Wealthy or eighth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Octavie usually hope their child will grow to embody wealthy or eighth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Οκταβία
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Οκταβία είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Octavia, που σημαίνει η όγδοη γεννημένη. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν κοινό μεταξύ των πρώτων χριστιανών και έχει μεγάλη σημασία στο πλαίσιο των νέων αρχών και της όγδοης ημέρας, που συμβολίζει την ανανέωση και την πληρότητα.

historical_references.reference: Octavie was a Christian martyr venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church. She was a slave girl who lived in Rome during the 3rd century AD. She was converted to Christianity by her master, and when her master died, she was sold to a new master who persecuted Christians. She refused to renounce her faith and was tortured and killed. Her feast day is celebrated on January 17.

Octavie was a Benedictine abbess in the Middle Ages. She was born in Normandy, France, around 1020 AD, and became a nun in the Benedictine monastery of Fécamp. She became abbess of the monastery around 1052 AD, and ruled until her death around 1080 AD. She was known for her piety, her generosity to the poor, and her efforts to reform the monastery.
